Conditional Expression

If sanctions reach energy flows or Nord Stream 2, own XLE and gold against European autos; Putin's claim that Nord Stream 2 would cement Europe's energy security, reported by Reuters [[n1087]], shows how central the pipeline is to Moscow's leverage. If measures stay financial, fade the energy spike and buy quality European exporters.
Risk

Moscow has threatened retaliation, with Sky News quoting Lavrov saying Russia would retaliate if the UK imposed new sanctions [[n1221]], and The New Yorker argued the threat of more sanctions may not deter Putin [[n1197]]. A counter-sanction on commodity exports would hit European industry hardest.

anticipatory.title: March FOMC: a quarter point or a half
parts: What Is Priced

Reuters' poll has a 25 bps March hike, with calls for 50 bps growing louder [[n1139]]. The 2Y at 1.47% (US Treasury, prior close 2022-02-18), up +46 bps in 20 observations, already embeds an aggressive path, and Reuters compiled what global banks forecast for Fed rate hikes in 2022 [[n1928]].
Conditional Expression

If Fed speakers lean toward a quarter point, in line with the New York Fed president's 'no need for a big hike' message [[n1930]], the 2Y can retrace and growth can outperform financials. If the front-loaded campaign that James Bullard again called for, per the WSJ [[n1153]], wins out, flatteners and short-duration value outperform.
Risk

A geopolitical growth shock could tempt the Fed to do less, but Al Jazeera reported the Fed is prepared for faster hikes if inflation persists [[n1911]], and Barron's examined how stocks perform just before and after a drastic Fed increase [[n0713]]. Governance adds noise: Politico reported Republicans delaying the vote on Biden's Fed nominees [[n1904]], leaving the Board's composition unsettled into the decision.

anticipatory.title: Home Depot and Lowe's: housing's spending test
parts: What Is Priced

Home Depot closed at 346.87 USD (-0.64% over 20 sessions) and Lowe's at 222.69 USD (-1.04%) (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), a modest discount given Reuters' preview that cooling home-improvement demand may pressure their 2022 sales [[n1029]].
Conditional Expression

A strong sales guide would validate the housing wealth effect, as Reuters reported existing home sales accelerating [[n1879]], and favour Home Depot over discretionary peers such as Target, which is -5.92% over 20 sessions at 204.39 USD. A cautious guide would confirm that mortgage rates at a 33-month high [[n1867]] are biting, and would argue for selling Lowe's against Home Depot rather than buying either.
Risk

The Guam Daily Post reported new-home construction falling 4.1% [[n1880]], while The Real Economy Blog said housing permits reached a 15-year high [[n1858]]. Fortune reported Zillow expecting home prices to spike 22% this spring [[n0652]], which supports ticket sizes, but NPR said first-time buyers are being squeezed out by investors [[n1874]]. Mixed housing signals make guidance, not the quarter, the swing factor, and a miss would reinforce the Bearish discretionary call.

anticipatory.title: An Iran nuclear deal and the oil premium
parts: What Is Priced

Brent at 93.54 USD/bbl and WTI at 91.07 USD/bbl (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) carry a Russia premium, and XLE's +8.97% 20-session gain to 68.05 USD embeds it in equities. The State Department said Iran talks are in their 'very final stages', Reuters reported [[n1217]].
Conditional Expression

A deal would release barrels with a lag, because Reuters reported the draft puts prisoners, enrichment and cash first, with oil coming later [[n1230]]. Express it by trimming refiners and the most oil-levered producers, not by exiting energy, since the Russia premium would still dominate. Shuttle diplomacy continues, with Al Jazeera reporting Iran's Raisi discussing the talks with Qatar's emir in Doha [[n1288]].
Risk

Al Jazeera reported Iran's parliament setting conditions for a return to the deal [[n1272]], and the OPEC+ ministerial line was to keep maintaining balance in oil markets [[n0125]]. A failed deal leaves Saudi Arabia's rejection of Biden's plea for more production, reported by The Intercept [[n1644]], as the binding constraint.

catalysts.title: General Dynamics (GD) — US armour for a frontline ally
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Reuters reported the US announced Abrams tanks for Poland as the Russia threat mounts [[n1375]], and DW said the US is set to sell them [[n1376]]. For US land-systems primes such as General Dynamics, an ally re-equipping on NATO's eastern flank converts geopolitical risk into backlog.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 215.82 USD, +0.66% on 18 February and +4.49% over 20 sessions, while ITA fell -0.84% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: defence budgets move slowly, and a diplomatic de-escalation would unwind the premium.
Trade Expression
Buy GD against ITA as a relative-value escalation hedge; add if the stock holds above 215.82 USD through the reopen, and cut if a Biden-Putin meeting is actually scheduled.

catalysts.title: Walmart (WMT) — the inflation share-taker
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

The WSJ said Walmart withstood pandemic blows and higher costs to boost business [[n1008]], and Al Jazeera described it thriving despite supply-chain woes and high inflation [[n0662]]. Grocery share gains [[n0661]] make it the defensive compounder in a stagflation scare.
Price Hurdle & Risk

Walmart closed at 137.99 USD, -0.64% on 18 February but +1.97% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: CNBC's report that shoppers are on alert as grocery bills climb [[n0664]] could cap volumes, and Reuters said Walmart's Mexico unit saw profit rise 5% while costs increased [[n0976]], the margin tension in miniature.
Trade Expression
Own WMT against XLY; add on a hold above 137.99 USD on the reopen. What changes the call: fuel and freight costs squeezing margins faster than prices can be raised.

catalysts.title: Home Depot (HD) — guidance over the quarter
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Home Depot's pending report arrives as Reuters warns cooling home-improvement demand may pressure 2022 sales [[n1029]]. The thesis is that professional customers and pricing protect margins even as do-it-yourself volumes normalise, while RetailWire's report that Yeti is leaving Lowe's to focus on direct sales [[n1023]] hints that brands are choosing channels more selectively.
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 346.87 USD, -0.31% on 18 February and -0.98% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: mortgage rates at their highest since May 2019 [[n1865]] slow housing turnover, the demand engine for renovation.
Trade Expression
Stay neutral into the print; buy on a guide that holds sales flat or higher with the stock above 346.87 USD, or sell Lowe's against it if guidance diverges.

catalysts.title: Nvidia (NVDA) — capacity bet versus multiple
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

NVIDIA's fourth-quarter and fiscal 2022 results [[n0084]] came with an upbeat revenue forecast [[n1661]], and TechSpot reported it spent $10 billion for a chunk of TSMC's 5nm capacity [[n1739]]: management is underwriting demand. The FTC said the termination of its Arm bid bodes well for competition [[n1674]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

The stock closed at 236.42 USD, -3.53% on 18 February and -1.28% over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk: the 2Y's +46 bps 20-observation rise compresses long-duration multiples faster than estimates rise, and AMD at 113.83 USD competes for the same data-centre budgets.
Trade Expression

Accumulate on weakness only while SOXX holds its +0.55% five-session gain, and avoid the levered SOXL (-9.33% over 20 sessions). What changes the call: a close back above the 233.74 USD level of 21 January would show the guide being rewarded.

catalysts.title: Intel (INTC) — the roadmap credibility discount
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Intel laid out an aggressive plan: PCWorld said its CPU roadmap spurs power efficiency [[n1703]], and CNET relayed Intel's claim that the chip technology for 2025 PCs is going great [[n1717]]. Fast Company's account of the $43.5B revival plan [[n0601]] signals heavy spending before returns, and the New York Times framed the question as whether Intel can make a comeback [[n0651]].
Price Hurdle & Risk

Intel closed at 45.04 USD, -5.32% on 18 February and -13.45% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Risk to the Bearish call: the $5.4 billion Tower Semiconductor acquisition [[n0298]] could accelerate foundry revenue.
Trade Expression
Underweight INTC against AMD (113.83 USD); reconsider above the 52.04 USD level of 21 January, which would show the market crediting the roadmap.

catalysts.title: Digital World Acquisition (DWAC) — Truth Social's launch test
parts: Catalyst & Thesis

Truth Social went live: Reuters reported it topped downloads on Apple's App Store with many users waitlisted [[n1610]], while Bloomberg said the app showed errors on launch day [[n1623]]. For DWAC, the SPAC for Trump Media & Technology Group, adoption is the valuation input.
Price Hurdle & Risk

DWAC closed at 84.32 USD on 18 February, -1.37% on the day but +15.32% over 20 sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), before the launch. Risk: Forbes described a glitchy start with thousands waitlisted [[n1613]], and the SPAC structure leaves merger-timing risk.
Trade Expression

Treat it as event-driven: hold only with a stop below 84.32 USD if the first post-launch session fails to extend. The next milestone is full operation by the end of March, which Nunes promised, per the Guardian [[n1604]].

spec.retail_intro: Retail finally gets to trade the long weekend, and its favourite story now has a scoreboard: Trump's Truth Social topped Apple's download chart and then parked users on a waitlist, a classic launch-day test in which curiosity is cheap and the first opening print decides whether early holders get paid.

retail.title: Digital World Acquisition / DWAC — top of the App Store, stuck in line
parts: Why Retail Is Here

Monday delivered what the DWAC crowd paid for, and what should worry it. Reuters reported that Truth Social topped downloads on Apple's App Store while many users were waitlisted [[n1610]], which moves the bull case from a promise to a scoreboard: a chart-topping app, the crowd reasons, has to be worth more than 84.32 USD, DWAC's last close on February 18 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The emotional hook has shifted from anticipation to vindication. The BBC framed the launch as Trump, banned from Twitter, returning with a new platform [[n1626]], and Sky News called it a bid for a social media comeback [[n1608]], the comeback story retail loves most because it doubles as revenge on the doubters. With US exchanges shut for the holiday, none of it is in the price yet.
What Is Driving It

The launch was real but rough. Reuters reported the app hitting the Apple store [[n1603]]; on Monday Forbes described a glitchy start with thousands on a waitlist [[n1613]], Bloomberg said it showed errors on launch day [[n1623]] and CBS called it a slow rollout [[n1621]]. That fits Nunes's own target of full operation by the end of March, per The Guardian [[n1604]]. Celebrity onboarding is the other engine: Forbes reports Sean Hannity and Marjorie Taylor Greene joined as the public struggled to sign up [[n1618]]. The backdrop is less friendly. DWAC's 15.32% gain over 20 sessions came while the Nasdaq 100 slipped 2.97% to 14,009.54 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and the market it reopens into must price a war risk that turned concrete on Monday evening, when Putin said Russia must recognise Ukraine's breakaway regions, per Reuters [[n0218]], and, in the Atlantic Council's words, Russia ordered troops into Ukraine again [[n1137]].
The Social Signal

This time attention comes with a ranking: Reuters' report that Truth Social topped Apple's downloads while many users were waitlisted [[n1610]] is a direct read on curiosity rather than a proxy. The explainer wave followed. Newsweek published a guide to joining and creating an account on iOS [[n1614]], PCMag ran an all-you-need-to-know primer on the network [[n1629]] and Business Insider a reporter's first-person test of the app [[n1615]]. For DWAC holders the waitlist is double-edged. Scarcity can read as demand on social feeds, but every user stuck in line is a download that has not yet become an active account.
Historical Analog

The closest recent rhyme is Coinbase's Super Bowl moment. ADWEEK says QR codes made waves at the game [[n0080]], and it now reports the Martin CEO publicly calling out Coinbase over its QR ad [[n0883]]; Coinbase closed at 189.16 USD, 2.76% lower over five sessions (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Interest that floods an app is a marketing win, not automatically a stock win. The general mechanism is the download-chart trap: a launch ranking measures curiosity on day one, while valuation depends on how many of those users are still posting months later, which no Monday chart can show.
Smart Money View

The professional mood is far gloomier than the download chart. Business Insider reports elite Wall Street investors saying privately that the market really did hit peak stupid and faces a cataclysmic shift that many will not survive [[n0788]], and Reuters that Wall Street banks fear inflation, asset-price deflation and even recession [[n0099]], the regime in which story stocks without earnings are de-rated first. Critics of the product are blunt: The Conversation calls Truth Social an ethically dubious Twitter for the right [[n1628]], and The Independent reports a little-known British company with an identical logo threatening legal action [[n1627]]. The bull counter is network effects: an app that opens at the top of the store with Hannity and Greene aboard [[n1618]] has a ready-made audience.
When the Narrative Breaks

Tuesday's open is the verdict. The bulls need DWAC to hold above the pre-launch 84.32 USD; a slide through the 73.12 USD of January 21 (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18) would erase the run-up and confirm a sell-the-news unwind. Watch the waitlist: if the glitchy start [[n1613]] stretches toward the end-of-March target [[n1604]], the scarcity story curdles into a capacity story, and the logo dispute is a small but concrete legal overhang [[n1627]]. The war gap matters more. Crypto, which trades around the clock and stayed open through Putin's address [[n1284]], fell on Monday, with Bitcoin down 3.53% to 37,075.28 USD and Solana down 8.56% (Yahoo Finance, prior completed daily close 2022-02-21), a hint that the first full US session may open risk-off and drag speculative tickers with it.

retail.title: Lockheed Martin / LMT — the war trade finally gets its trigger
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The war trade's logic is the simplest on the board, and the grimmest: if armies move, governments buy missiles and jets, so own the companies that build them. Monday evening supplied the trigger. Reuters reports Putin saying Russia must recognise Ukraine's breakaway regions [[n0218]], and the Atlantic Council writes that Russia just ordered troops into Ukraine again [[n1137]]. Lockheed Martin last closed at 386.46 USD, up 4.11% over 20 sessions, with Raytheon Technologies up 7.06% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), while additional US F-15s are sent to Poland to bolster NATO's eastern flank (The National Interest) [[n1367]].
Where It Breaks

The awkward fact is that the trade has not worked while fear built: Lockheed fell 2.46% over five sessions and the ITA aerospace and defense ETF slipped 0.84% to 104.30 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), while Rheinmetall dropped 2.70% to 93.84 EUR on Monday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Defense budgets move over years, not news cycles, so a Tuesday pop can fade as fast as it comes, and Beijing's renewed sanctions on Lockheed and Raytheon over Taiwan arms sales (Reuters) [[n0794]] show geopolitics cuts both ways. If LMT cannot hold a gain above 386.46 USD, the war trade is being sold, not bought.

retail.title: China Internet ETF / KWEB — the bargain Beijing keeps repricing
parts: Why Retail Is Here

The bargain hunter's case for Chinese tech is simple: the banks say buy, and Beijing's giants are outlasting the US platform retail just watched collapse. CNBC reported investment banks from Credit Suisse to Goldman Sachs saying it is time to buy Chinese stocks [[n0155]], and Business Insider that Tencent joined the world's ten most valuable companies as Meta slid on its stock rout [[n0561]]. Meta Platforms (FB) closed at 206.16 USD, down 32.00% over 20 sessions, while KWEB, the one-ticker China internet basket, closed at 35.60 USD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The swap feels like contrarian common sense.
Where It Breaks

The discount exists for a reason Beijing keeps renewing. The WSJ reported China ordering cuts to food-delivery fees, sparking a tech selloff [[n0693]], and Bloomberg that the policy wiped $26 billion off Meituan's value [[n0694]]; KWEB fell 5.04% on February 18 and Alibaba's US shares 4.37% (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). The slide carried into Monday in Hong Kong, where Tencent lost 5.23% to 423.03 HKD (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21). Reuters reports Washington put Tencent- and Alibaba-run sites on its notorious-markets list [[n0200]], and Caixin says Hillhouse ditched Alibaba [[n0324]]. If KWEB opens below 35.60 USD and keeps sliding, the bargain is a value trap.

retail.title: 3x Nasdaq 100 ETF / TQQQ — the YOLO dip-buy meets a war gap
parts: Why Retail Is Here

YOLO now has a strategy page: Yahoo Finance calls it the new investment strategy raking in millions for young investors, though it remains risky [[n0825]]. With Fortune asking how low tech stocks can fall [[n0803]], the YOLO version of buy-the-dip is TQQQ, which closed at 50.44 USD, down 3.39% on February 18 and 10.99% over 20 sessions, against a 1.14% fall for the unlevered QQQ (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18). Three times the bounce feels like a shortcut back to even.
Where It Breaks

This time the dip arrives as a gap. TQQQ last traded before Putin's address, with the VIX at 27.75 index points (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-18), and Europe has since fallen, the DAX down 2.07% on Monday (Yahoo Finance, prior close 2022-02-21); a lower open hands holders roughly three times the index damage before they can react. AdvisorHub reports a popular broker-dealer charged over leveraged ETF sales that cost clients $2.3M [[n1587]].
